content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a\", \"title\": \"Close-out register conventions\", \"name\": \"Close-out register conventions\", \"revisionId\": \"8b9413d402\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-13T16:38:02Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T16:58:40Z\", \"text\": \"Close-out register conventions\\n1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.\\n2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.\\n3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors \\u2014 each account there gets its own row.\\n4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.\\n5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) \\u2014 say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.\\n6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage \\u2014 ads, cloud \\u2014 use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends \\u2014 then the day before it ends.\\n7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.\\n8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual \\u00f7 12, quarterly \\u00f7 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.\\n9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).\\n10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a", "title": "Close-out register conventions", "name": "Close-out register conventions", "revisionId": "8b9413d402", "createdTime": "2026-02-13T16:38:02Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T16:58:40Z", "text": "Close-out register conventions
1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.
2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.
3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors — each account there gets its own row.
4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.
5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) — say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.
6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage — ads, cloud — use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends — then the day before it ends.
7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.
8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual ÷ 12, quarterly ÷ 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.
9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).
10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.
"}

Hi Leonard, Robert, Arthur,

Thanks for signing today. Before we can deliver the licensed data set, these accounts need to stay active with their full history and every user in place until we confirm delivery: Slack (stay on the paid plan — the free plan hides history older than 90 days), Google Workspace (every user account, including former staff — please don't archive or delete any), Figma, Linear, GitHub and Metabase. Nothing on this list should be closed, downgraded or archived before the delivery review call Leonard booked with us. Accounts that aren't on the list aren't part of the licensed bundle, so close them whenever suits you.

For Helpshift, please export the full ticket history to Drive before your subscription ends.

If our engineers change anything on this list, we'll reply on this thread.

Best,
Maya

Maya

Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,
Leonard", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1770664152.207829", "type": "message", "text": "this covers all the topics I guess", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1770664094.831769", "type": "message", "text": "email to [PERSON_NAME_1999]: Hi [PERSON_NAME_1999],

Total cost is $300/month more or less\\n\\u2022 I\\u2019ll contact [ORG_NAME_0304] to let them stop from auto-renewing (next auto-renew is Nov 26 so we have time)\\n\\u2022 Anything else I\\u2019m missing? \", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770933601.686309\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"During shutdown, let\\u2019s keep Deel, gusto, Intuit. Figma won\\u2019t be able to charge us by the time it\\u2019s time for renewal. linear we keep during transition\", \"channel\": \"C0ADGSZKR3R\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1770933601.686309\"}, {\"ts\": \"1770932503.543519\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"and this is for Singular\\n\\nHi [PERSON_NAME_8008] and Singular team,\\nWe have unfortunate news. Harmony Games Inc. is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.\\nBecause of this, we need to terminate our agreement with Singular effective immediately. Register's done and shared with you and Arthur as editors: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QOpZNEAmRXiXpV078ZtcaGcp1Soo19GsJMxfis_LfDI/edit

*Monthly totals*
• All 25 rows (what it costs us today): *$6,706.49/mo*
• Keep + Hold rows only (what's left after the plan): *$1,249.04/mo*

*Clash with what we already decided*
• *Google Workspace:* the Feb 12 plan has you archiving Google accounts after Feb 15. Sunset's checklist says every Workspace user, former staff included, stays active (no archiving, no deleting) until the delivery review on Mar 12. Archiving after the 15th would break that, so I've marked it Hold for Sunset to Mar 12. It's on the SVB card, so billing still has to move off by EOD Feb 17.
• *Worth a check, Slack:* on Feb 11 we said "free version" and then moved people to guests. Sunset needs the paid plan, full history and every user in place. *How the rest landed*
• Sunset's Feb 13 update adds Trello, BigQuery and dbt to the hold list and drops Metabase. Metabase stays a move to Arthur's LLC.
• Gusto is Cancel per Arthur's reply under the keep list.
• Unity is Closed: their account manager confirmed, and there's no invoice on the 19th.
• Every open cancellation is due EOD Feb 17, except Carta (Aug 14, per your exemption).
• Still waiting on confirmation from: Singular, Layer, CodeRabbit.
• Still to cancel: Gusto, Docusign, 1Password, ElevenLabs.
• I added ElevenLabs from the costs-tab Sound line ($50/yr, ENG-2467, mine). Pond5 ended in Sep, so it's not on the list.
• Canceled in Linear: Intuit (same account as QuickBooks), Lucidchart (expired Nov), iPostal (mailbox cancelled Jan 16), Google Ads (ad account).
• Every Linear issue has a comment saying where it stands and what happens next.

content.text:
The account close-out register is built and shared with Leonard and Arthur as editors. Every Linear issue is settled with a comment, and I've replied in Leonard's #winddown thread.

**Register:** [Account close-out register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QOpZNEAmRXiXpV078ZtcaGcp1Soo19GsJMxfis_LfDI/edit). It has 25 rows and follows the rules in Leonard's conventions doc. It's in your My Drive, because I didn't have permission to move it into the Wind Down folder.
- **What it all costs today:** $6,706.49/mo
- **What's left after the plan (Keep + Hold rows):** $1,249.04/mo

**Clash I flagged to Leonard:** his own Feb 12 plan has him archiving Google accounts after Feb 15. Sunset's data checklist says every Google Workspace user, former staff included, has to stay active until their Mar 12 delivery review. I marked Google as "Hold for Sunset" until Mar 12.

**Also flagged, as worth checking rather than a clash:** on Feb 11, Arthur agreed to drop Slack to the free plan, and Leonard turned most members into guests. Sunset needs Slack kept on the paid plan with every user in place. I suggested he confirm with Sunset that guests count.

**What changed from the original plan:**
- Sunset's Feb 13 update adds Trello, BigQuery and dbt to their keep list and drops Metabase, which stays moved to Arthur's LLC.
- Gusto is now Cancel, per Arthur's reply under the keep list.
- Unity is closed: their account manager confirmed there's no Feb 19 invoice.
- SVB closes the card on the 18th, so open cancellations, and moving kept accounts off the card, are due by end of day Feb 17. Carta is the exception (Aug 14), as Leonard said.

**Linear:**
- **Done (6):** Unity, Helpshift, Cursor, Zapier, Kapwing, Soundly.
- **Canceled (4):** Intuit (same account as QuickBooks), Lucidchart (expired Nov 2025), iPostal (cancelled Jan 16), Google Ads (ad account, which Leonard is closing himself).
- **Left open:** everything else.
- **New:** ENG-2467 for ElevenLabs. I found it inside the costs-tab "Sound" line ($50/yr), so under Leonard's rules it's yours.

**Still on you by end of day Feb 17:** cancel Docusign and ElevenLabs.

**Left off the register:** two $30/mo game-ops lines that Arthur said he's handling himself (they look like people or contractors), and Calendly ($96/yr). Neither was in Arthur's Linear project, and the conventions only asked me to add accounts hidden inside lines that cover several vendors. If you think Calendly belongs, it's a quick row to add.
